## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | MEDIUM |
| Task Type | Verification preflight correctness and policy propagation |
| Complexity | STANDARD |

### What Was Claimed

Malformed root `package.json` test metadata could cause verification setup to select a nested package instead of the repository root. The remediation must treat malformed root `scripts.test` values as invalid, avoid nested-package inference, fall back to CI-only verification, add regression coverage, and review the exact remediation head.

### What We Found

`src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` resolves only the explicitly configured command cwd, so it does not currently walk or select a nested package. It validates a package script by requiring a non-empty string, but any non-string root `scripts.test` value currently raises `VerificationPreflightError` and aborts startup. The existing test fixture contains a valid nested package and covers a missing root script, but does not cover root `scripts.test` values that are objects or arrays.

The startup path invokes preflight before launching the writer, then passes `policy.verification.commands` into direct and nested bindings. Recovery and parent-node paths reload policy, so a CI-only decision made at startup would be lost unless it is recorded on the active run link and reapplied to every later policy snapshot. The subagent task and verification logic already define an empty local command map as valid CI-only mode, while GitHub CI remains parent-owned and required by the tracked staging policy.

### Root Cause

The preflight contract has no typed result for a malformed root test script and no durable representation of the resulting CI-only mode. Consequently, the only current outcome is a startup error, and there is no way to propagate an intentional local-check disablement through child bindings, recovery, refresh, or parent-owned verification aggregation. The safe fix is to classify present malformed root `scripts.test` metadata separately from genuinely missing/invalid required configuration, return an explicit CI-only result with an empty command map, and persist that mode on the run link.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Classify malformed root test metadata and return an explicit preflight mode/result. |
| `src/core/policy.ts` | Provide an immutable helper for applying the effective local command map to the trusted policy snapshot. |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Apply and persist CI-only mode at startup and reapply it during recovery, refresh, reconciliation, and integration. |
| `src/adapters/subagents.ts` | Carry the explicit verification mode into direct/nested/refresh bindings. |
| `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` | Validate and retain the bound mode while enforcing that CI-only bindings have no local commands. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Add object/array malformed-root regressions and result assertions. |
| `test/core/policy.test.ts` | Cover immutable effective-policy propagation. |
| `README.md` | Document malformed root test metadata as CI-only fallback. |
| `DESIGN.md` | Align the verification trust-boundary contract with the explicit fallback. |

### Evidence

- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` currently returns `Promise<void>` and `assertPackageScript` throws whenever the selected package has no non-empty string script.
- `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory` canonicalizes and bounds the configured cwd; no nested-package discovery exists in the current implementation.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` has a root package without `scripts.test` and a nested `web/package.json` with a valid test script, but no malformed object/array root values.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` constructs bindings from `policy.verification.commands` at startup and reloads policy for direct recovery, parent nodes, reconciliation, integration, and finalization.
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts` explicitly describes an empty command map as valid CI-only verification and delegates GitHub CI enforcement to the parent.
- Tracked README guidance currently says missing scripts fail closed and `commands: {}` is CI-only; it must distinguish genuinely missing scripts from malformed root test metadata per the supervisor-approved issue decision.

### History Findings

- Issue #114 records the prior review finding `INIT-MONO-001` from PR #110 and identifies remediation commit `d174f8e9d8ff88c1a40b8a75c99489c76ef52e92` as the intended behavior: malformed `scripts.test` values are invalid, nested selection is avoided, and verification falls back to CI-only with regression coverage.
- The current integration branch contains the strict non-string script check and missing-root regression, but not the typed CI-only propagation contract required by this run.

### Recommendation

Add a typed `local`/`ci-only` preflight result. For a required command whose explicitly selected repository-root `scripts.test` property is present but malformed (including object or array values), validate executable and cwd safety, classify the result as CI-only, and return an empty effective local command map without discovering another package. Continue failing closed for unavailable executables, invalid/missing package manifests, genuinely absent required scripts, unsafe cwd values, and malformed non-root package configuration. Carry the mode through the immutable policy snapshot, active run link, child bindings, recovery, and all parent verification aggregation paths. Add focused regressions and update documentation.

### Related Issues

- #94 — source issue referenced by the review finding.
- #110 — source pull request containing the original finding.
- #114 — current remediation issue.

### Decomposition Assessment

**Required**: no — this is one bounded verification-preflight and propagation change across its direct policy, workflow, binding, documentation, and test seams. No product, UX, branch-authority, or security-authority decision remains after the supervisor-approved fallback decision.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Root `scripts.test` object metadata is treated as malformed and returns explicit CI-only mode without selecting the valid nested package.
- [ ] Root `scripts.test` array metadata is treated the same way.
- [ ] The effective policy and every child/recovery binding contain no local commands in CI-only mode.
- [ ] Missing scripts, invalid manifests, unavailable executables, unsafe paths, and malformed non-root package metadata retain fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage passes, followed by the required full `check` verification and exact-head fresh correctness/security review.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Prevent malformed repository-root `scripts.test` metadata from selecting or executing a nested package. Treat a present malformed root test value (including object or array data) as a typed CI-only fallback, propagate that mode through the trusted startup policy and every child/recovery binding, and preserve fail-closed behavior for genuinely missing or unsafe required configuration.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `src/core/policy.ts`
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts`
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `test/core/policy.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts`
- `test/agents/child-runtime.test.ts`
- `README.md`
- `DESIGN.md`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not add nested-package discovery, implicit cwd selection, or package-manager-specific bypasses.
- Do not weaken path, executable, manifest, command argv, lease, GitHub CI, review, merge, or child-containment authority checks.
- Do not make malformed non-root package metadata silently pass.
- Do not alter issue/PR writes, branch policy, reviewer requirements, or merge/close/cleanup behavior.
- Do not change unrelated source, fixtures, dependencies, generated artifacts, or `.pi/forge` runtime output.

### Invariants

- Only an explicitly configured cwd may be inspected; a malformed root test script never causes a nested cwd to be selected.
- A root `scripts.test` property is malformed when it is present but not a non-empty string; root `scripts` metadata that is not an object is also malformed for this classification.
- A genuinely absent required root script, invalid package JSON, missing package manifest, unavailable executable, unsafe/missing cwd, or malformed non-root package remains fail-closed.
- CI-only mode always has an empty effective local verification command map and leaves GitHub CI policy unchanged.
- Policy snapshots are immutable; recovery cannot re-enable commands that startup disabled.
- Existing valid root and explicitly configured nested package checks retain their behavior.

### Deliverables

- Typed preflight result with `local`/`ci-only` mode and effective command map.
- Immutable helper to apply the effective map to a trusted `ForgePolicy` snapshot.
- Durable active-link and child-binding propagation with strict CI-only binding validation.
- Focused object/array root metadata regressions, propagation tests, and documentation updates.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| ROOT-OBJECT | Classify root `scripts.test: { ... }` as CI-only and return no local commands. |
| ROOT-ARRAY | Classify root `scripts.test: [ ... ]` as CI-only and return no local commands. |
| NO-NESTED | Keep cwd resolution explicit and prove a valid nested package is not selected as fallback. |
| PROPAGATION | Apply the preflight result to the policy and carry the mode through active links, RPC launches, direct bindings, recovery, refresh, and parent aggregation. |
| FAIL-CLOSED | Retain errors for absent required scripts, invalid manifests, unavailable executables, unsafe paths, and non-root malformed package metadata. |
| REGRESSION | Extend focused adapter/policy/binding tests and run the required `check` command. |
| DOCS | Document malformed-root CI-only fallback while preserving explicit `commands: {}` semantics. |

### Out of Scope

- Changing tracked `.forge/config.json` for this repository.
- Discovering package workspaces or inferring package roots.
- Altering GitHub CI check discovery or merge gating.
- Adding a new verification command or package-manager integration.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- PR #110 review finding `INIT-MONO-001` identified malformed root test metadata as a monorepo selection hazard.
- Issue #114 cites remediation commit `d174f8e9d8ff88c1a40b8a75c99489c76ef52e92`; this run completes the typed CI-only startup and propagation behavior on the current integration base.
- Existing preflight tests already cover explicit nested package cwd success, missing root script failure, executable checks, and symlink/path safety.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` loads trusted policy, prepares the frozen worktree, and preflights required commands before initializing/launching the run.
- `SubagentsRpcClient` serializes policy verification commands into top-level, bounded-node, reviewer, and refresh bindings.
- `ForgeChildBinding` gates `forge_verify`; empty commands drive the existing valid CI-only writer instruction.
- Active run recovery, node reconciliation, integration, refresh, and finalization reload policy and must reapply the persisted mode before aggregating local checks or dispatching children.

### CI Surface

- `.forge/config.json` requires `check` locally and GitHub CI on `staging`.
- CI-only mode disables local commands only; parent-owned GitHub CI remains required and is checked against the exact reviewed head before merge.
- The named local verification command is `check` (`npm run check`), with no additional local allowlist.

### Prior Findings

- Existing code strictly requires a non-empty string package script but aborts startup for malformed root metadata.
- Existing README/DESIGN text says missing scripts fail closed and `commands: {}` is CI-only; wording must distinguish malformed-root fallback from genuinely missing required scripts.

### Hazards

- Passing only an empty command map without a mode would make recovery indistinguishable from a naturally CI-only policy and could allow a reload to restore commands.
- A shallow policy mutation would violate trusted snapshot expectations; clone only the verification object and preserve all other policy fields.
- CI-only bindings containing commands must be rejected to prevent contradictory child authority.
- Optional commands and valid explicitly configured nested packages must not accidentally become startup blockers or fallback targets.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Refactor verification preflight to inspect package metadata strictly at the configured cwd, classify malformed root test metadata separately, return `{ mode, commands, reason }`, and retain fail-closed errors for all other required failures. (ROOT-OBJECT, ROOT-ARRAY, NO-NESTED, FAIL-CLOSED)
2. Add an immutable policy helper for replacing the effective local command map and extend the active run link with persisted verification mode. (PROPAGATION)
3. Apply the effective policy at startup and on every loaded-policy recovery/dispatch/integration/finalization path; pass mode through RPC launch inputs and direct/refresh bindings. (PROPAGATION)
4. Validate binding mode and command-map consistency in the child runtime; preserve the existing no-local-commands CI-only writer path. (PROPAGATION, FAIL-CLOSED)
5. Add focused root object/array, policy, RPC/binding, and fail-closed regressions; update README and DESIGN wording. (REGRESSION, DOCS)
6. Review the assigned diff, run the required named `check`, commit implementation, prepare the exact PR head, and perform the fresh correctness/security review panel. (REGRESSION)

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
